transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... honestly, something's been happening at work that really scared me. I work in a surveillance room, and lately, during the quiet stretches, I've been hearing voices coming through the monitor speakers. 

They say things to me, like, you missed it, Ruth, or... people are going to get hurt because of you. But the thing is, I know every channel is muted. And no one else in the room hears anything at all. That's what finally scared me enough to come in and see someone.
Have you noticed any other unusual experiences, like seeing things that aren't there, feeling sensations on your skin, or anything else that others around you don't seem to notice?

No, um... no, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't see things that aren't there, and I haven't had any weird feelings on my skin or anything. It's really just... just the voices from the monitors. That's the only unusual thing that's been happening.
When you hear the voices, are there any external sounds or stimuli happening at the same time that could explain them?

No, there really isn't. Like I mentioned, it usually happens during the quiet stretches in the surveillance room. There's no static, no background noise, nothing like that. 

It's just quiet, and I know for a fact every channel is completely muted. That's what makes it stand out so much when I hear it coming through the speakers, saying things like, "You missed it, Ruth," or telling me people are going to get hurt because of me. There's just no other sound happening in the room that could explain it.
When you hear the voices coming through the monitors, do they feel like they're coming from inside your head or from the actual speakers?

They definitely sound like they're coming from the actual speakers. That's... that's why it's so unsettling. It doesn't feel like a thought in my head at all. I hear the voices coming right through the monitor speakers, clear as day, saying, "You missed it, Ruth," or telling me people are going to get hurt because of me. But like I said, I know the channels are muted, and my coworkers don't hear a thing. It's really what scared me enough to make this appointment.
Have you had any thoughts that something about these voices might be part of a larger plan or conspiracy, like someone trying to send you a message or control what you do?

No, I haven't really thought anything like that. I don't feel like anyone is trying to control me or send me some kind of secret message. It's just... it's just the voices themselves. They just say those terrible things about me messing up, but I don't think it's part of a conspiracy or anything bigger. It's just happening to me, and I don't know why.
Have you ever believed something to be true that others around you don’t seem to believe, especially related to the voices you’ve been hearing?

Well, I don't know if it's something others don't believe, but... I do believe that I'm just fundamentally careless. I keep replaying every missed camera angle or delayed call in my head, like... like it's proof that I'm dangerous to the people I'm supposed to be watching out for. The voices say it, but I feel it too. Part of me really believes I deserve to be punished if anything goes wrong on my watch because I'm just so worthless at my job.
Have you ever had any strong beliefs that something is true—like something serious is wrong with you or someone is out to get you—that your family or friends don't share or understand?

No, not really. I don't think anyone is out to get me, or that I have some kind of hidden disease or anything like that. My family knows I've been really down lately, and they usually just tell me I'm being too hard on myself when I talk about how bad I am at my job. But I don't have any strong beliefs about people being after me or something serious being wrong with my body, no. It's really just what I mentioned before about work.
Have you ever had a belief that something was definitely true about your work performance, even when others told you it wasn't, like missing something important when others said everything was fine?

Yeah, I guess that's exactly it. People at work, my supervisor... they tell me I'm doing fine, that the shift went smoothly. But I just don't believe them. I keep replaying every single missed camera angle or delayed call in my head over and over. To me, it's just proof that I'm completely careless and actually dangerous to the people I'm supposed to be protecting. It doesn't matter what anyone else says. I just know I'm messing up, and honestly, part of me believes I deserve to be punished if anything goes wrong on my watch.
Have you ever been absolutely certain about something that wasn’t true, like thinking you definitely made a mistake that you actually didn’t, even though others told you otherwise?

No, I don't think so. I mean, other than what I just said about work. I'm not imagining mistakes that didn't actually happen. The delayed calls or the camera angles I mentioned... those are real things that happen on my shift. 

It's just that my supervisor says they aren't a big deal or that everything is fine, but I know it's not. So I haven't been certain about a mistake that was completely made up, no. Just... just what I already told you.

Have you ever believed, with absolute certainty, that the voices you heard were trying to tell you something important about reality that others just didn't understand, or that they revealed a hidden truth about yourself or the world?

No, I don't hear voices. I've never heard anyone talking to me when there wasn't someone actually there. So, no, I haven't had any voices telling me hidden truths or anything like that. It's just my own thoughts about work, like I explained.
Have you had these strong feelings of guilt or worthlessness about your work for a long time, or do they come and go depending on how your shifts go?

They don't really come and go. It's just... constant now. This has been going on for about four months. It started right around the time I was moved into the lead casino surveillance role. Ever since then, it's just been this heavy feeling all the time.
Even though your supervisor says you're doing fine, do you still feel certain that you're performing poorly at work, in a way that feels unshakable to you?

Yeah, I do. I know he says everything is fine, but... I just know I'm failing. It doesn't really matter how many times he tells me I'm doing okay. I just have this... this absolute certainty that I'm messing it up, and it just doesn't go away.

Have you ever had any beliefs that most people would find completely unrealistic or strange, like thinking something was happening that wasn't, or that something was wrong with you in a way that didn’t make sense to others?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't have any strange beliefs like that. It's really just this overwhelming feeling that I'm completely failing at my job, and the guilt that comes with it. But I don't think things are happening that aren't, or anything bizarre like that. It's just the work stuff.

Have you ever had any beliefs that others found completely strange or unrealistic, like thinking something was happening that wasn’t, or that something was wrong with you in a way that didn’t make sense to them?

Um, I think you might have just asked me that, but... no. Like I said a second ago, I don't have any strange ideas like that. It's really just the work situation and feeling like a complete failure. I don't think anything bizarre is happening to me, or anything like what you're describing.

Have you ever had any beliefs about things in your life—like your job performance or something else—that you were completely sure were true, even when there wasn’t clear evidence, or when others didn’t share that belief?

Well, yes, about work. I'm a surveillance officer, so I watch the cameras all day. I just... I keep replaying every missed camera angle or delayed call in my head. To me, it's just proof that I'm careless and, honestly, dangerous. I'm completely sure of it. Part of me really believes I deserve to be punished if anything goes wrong on my watch, because it's all my fault.
